# Information-processing capacity — findings (reservoir-intrinsic capability)

*Generated by `information_capacity.py` (`cli.py run capacity`). Tests the strongest remaining
place a genuine quantum-RC advantage could hide: does the quantum reservoir's 2ⁿ Hilbert space
buy **more nonlinear information-processing capacity** than a matched classical reservoir,
**decoupled from the (linear-dominated) RV task**?*

Method (Information-Processing-Capacity probe, Dambre et al. 2012 style): iid input
u∼Uniform[−1,1], delay-embed the last n values (every model gets the SAME window, scaled to [0,1]
for fair angle-encoding/kernel input); target basis = Legendre-polynomial products of the lagged
inputs grouped by total degree (1 = linear memory, 2/3 = nonlinear); capacity for a target =
out-of-sample R² of a ridge readout on the reservoir features (clipped [0,1]); capacity-by-degree
= Σ R². Matched feature count (n + n(n−1)/2 = 55 at n=10). 3 seeds.

## Results (n=10, T=3000, mean over 3 seeds; basis: 8 linear, 8 deg-2, 4 deg-3)

| model | linear (d1) | nonlin (d2) | nonlin (d3) | **NONLINEAR total** | TOTAL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **CHIMERA** | 6.06 | 2.76 | 0.01 | **2.77** | 8.82 |
| RFF (RBF)   | 7.36 | 3.45 | 0.07 | **3.51** | 10.88 |
| ESN         | 7.82 | 2.88 | 0.02 | **2.89** | 10.71 |

## Verdict

**The quantum reservoir does NOT have higher capacity — it is *lower* on every axis** (nonlinear
2.77 vs RFF 3.51 / ESN 2.89; total 8.82 vs 10.88 / 10.71), consistently across seeds. At matched
feature count and identical input, the Pauli-Z feature map of the fixed Ising reservoir spans a
*less* flexible function space than a random-Fourier RBF map or an echo-state reservoir.

**Why this matters (it deepens the honest negative):** the no-advantage result on realized
volatility is not merely "the task doesn't reward the quantum reservoir's extra expressivity" —
**there is no extra expressivity to reward.** Even on a clean, task-independent capability
benchmark the quantum reservoir is not more (indeed somewhat less) nonlinearly expressive than
matched classical maps at simulable scale. This closes the most plausible remaining route to a
defensible quantum advantage in this paper, and explains mechanistically why a linear model (HAR-X)
wins on a linear-long-memory-dominated target.

*Scope:* one fixed reservoir family (transverse-field Ising, τ=2, conn 0.5) at n=10; a different
Hamiltonian/encoding could differ, but V2-B1 already showed train-KTA-optimal reservoir selection
makes out-of-sample *worse*, so tuning is not a free lever. The honest reading is robust.
